textbookText: 8.2.7 PHYLUM ARTHROPODA Artheopoda (Gr; arthros-jointed; podo-foot) is the largest phylum of animal kingdom which consists of more than 800000 species found in all types of habitat. These animals comprise about 80% of all known animals.
1. They are the most diversified animals inhabiting the land, water and air. They are mostly free living and some of them are parasites of both plants and animals.
2. Body is bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and metamerically segmented. 3. Body segments bear jointed appendages which are variously modified such as jaws,

antenna, gills etc. Legs are adapted for walking, swimming, food capturing, tearing of food, defense etc. 4. They have organ system level of body organization. 5. Their coelom is true but reduced and filled with blood called haemocoelom. 6. Body is externally covered by thick chitionous and tough layer of cuticle which act as exoskeleton, secreted by underlying epidermis. Cuticle cast off periodically during growth and development and this process is called moulting or ecdysis. 7. Body is distinctly divided into three regions-head, thorax and abdomen. However, head and thorax is fused to form cephalothorax in some cases such as prawn, spider. 8. Muscular layer is not continuous but lie as separate bundles below epidermis which allows rapid contraction during movements. 9. Respiratory organs are booklungs and trachea in terrestrial forms and gills in aquatic forms. Some of them also respire through general body surface. 10. Digestive system is complete with mouth and anus at the opposite ends. Mouth is surrounded by a number of appendages called mouth parts which are adapted variously for bitting, chewing, sucking etc. 11. Excretion takes place through malpighian tubules or coelomoducts or green glands or coxal glands. 12. They have open type of circulatory system which consists of dorsally placed heart, arteries and blood sinuses or lacunae. There are no veins and capillaries. 13. Nervous system is typically annelidan type that consists of dorsal brain with nerve ring and ganglionated ventral nerve cord with lateral nerves. 14. Sensory organs are simple eyes, compound eyes, antenna, hairs, statocyst, and auditory organs. These organs perceive stimuli like light, chemical, touch, sound etc. and also help in maintaining body posture during locomotion. 15. Compound eye is composed of many visual units or lenses called ommatidia and such eye can detect very slowly moving object. 16. They are usually unisexual and well-marked sexual dimorphism is found in most cases. 17. Fertilization is mostly internal. Development is direct and indirect both. Parental care is also found in some arthropods. 18. Parthenogenesis occurs in some cases.
